newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCC rates stay low, chartering slows.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCC rates stay low, chartering slows.

text.p: Middle East spot tanker rates remained at the lower levels posted last week amid a dearth of fresh VLCC fixtures and an abundance of tonnage, London brokers said on Monday.
Activity was subdued by the U.S. Labor Day holiday, they said.
Some brokers said they expected VLCC rates to improve toward the end of the month if chartering activity picks up.
VLCCs bound for Japan stayed on last done levels of W65, whilst western voyages were still only able to command W55, also unchanged.
By late afternoon, no fresh Mideast Gulf VLCC fixtures had been reported.
A meagre three charters had been seen on Monday with 80,000 tonne LR2s travelling both to the west and east, fixed by Vitol, Mobil and Elf.

"It seems highly likely that (VLCC) rate levels will take on an upwards bias this month due to there being (only) 74 units of (a combined) 21 million deadweight tonnes available between now and the latter stages of September," one broker said.
In the inter-UKC sector, rates on 80,000 tonners remained on an equilibrium around W100, as evidenced by Total's chartering of the Solena at W100.
Western hemisphere and Caribbean rates settled on last done levels, with 70,000 tonners travelling up the U.S. coast able to command in the region of W130.
The blitzkrieg of hurricanes, Edouard and Fran, which threatened shipping in the region last Friday, has eased considerably, with no further vessels delayed.
